newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MANCHESTER UNITED V LIVERPOOL FACTS AND FIGURES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MANCHESTER UNITED V LIVERPOOL FACTS AND FIGURES.

text.p: Facts and figures for Saturday's English premier league match between Manchester United and Liverpool:
Manchester United: Formed 1878 as Newton Heath, changed name to Manchester United 1902.

Major honours: European Champions 1968; European Cup Winners Cup winners 1991; English League champions 1908, 1911, 1952, 1956, 1957, 1965, 1967, 1993, 1994, 1996; F.A. Cup Winners 1909, 1948, 1963, 1977, 1983, 1985, 1990, 1994, 1996; League Cup winners 1992.
Record League goalscorer: Bobby Charlton 199 goals
Most capped player: Bobby Charlton, England 106, 1958-70
Record League goalscorer: Roger Hunt 245 goals 1959-69
Most capped player: Ian Rush, Wales 73, 1980-94
Manchester United v Liverpool league record:
First league meeting: December 25, 1906: Manchester United 0 Liverpool 0, English division one (clubs had met in 1890s when United were still known as Newton Heath)
Manchester United 6, Liverpool 1, Old Trafford, May 5, 1928
Last 10 seasons at Old Trafford from 1986-87 (Manchester United score first) 1-0, 1-1, 3-1, 1-2, 1-1, 0-0, 2-2, 1-0, 2-0, 2-2.
Corresponding match last season: October 1, 1995, Manchester United 2 (Nicky Butt, Eric Cantona pen.) Liverpool 2 (Robbie Fowler 2), Attendance 34,934

Fascinating fact: Although Liverpool and United have almost identical records against each other in the league Manchester United have a far superior record in the F.A. Cup. Of their 13 F.A. Cup matches, United have won seven, including two cup finals. There have been four draws and Liverpool have won just twice, the last occasion back in 1921.
